items.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: I think Jimmy Giuffre used a B flat half diminished.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Yeah. As a matter of fact that’s where I first started to write. I started writing in the service mainly through the small tools that I had learned at the Schillinger House. And I mean they seem so simple today, but they were such invaluable tools, you know, and then I would start copying a lot of records, like I remember taking “Four Others” off the record and how I would do is I would figure out what the harmony is, then I could hear if it was closed or open voicing, and I could hear that and I could…
which I kind of liked better — blowing my own horn now — [scats] I think the second chord I use in “Four Others,” I use an E seventh chord and I think Jimmy Giuffre used a B flat half diminished.
